nodes.label: Do Not Do List
nodes.rationale: You make money by doing stuff but get rich by what you don't do; list what you hate doing, then the only options are let it go undone, delegate it to someone who loves it, or keep doing it and miss your target. Doing what you hate is the riskiest thing a founder can do.

nodes.label: Eight Business Drivers
nodes.rationale: Reverse-engineered categories of what makes businesses work long term: marketing (attention + reputation), sales (monetization + certainty), offer (desire + fulfillment), finance, team, balance, mind work, retention.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Energy Over Time
nodes.rationale: Energy is a superior resource to time; burnout comes from running out of energy, and 'I need to work harder' is the wrong reflex; winners quit games whose outcome they no longer care about.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Engage Not Escape
nodes.rationale: The entrepreneur's job is to engage in what they could do for hours without running out of energy, not to escape the business; backfill yourself out of what you hate and plug into what you love.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Execution Attachment
nodes.rationale: Operator mindset of doing everything yourself under the excuse of quality; suppresses operational leverage and makes the business unsellable.

nodes.label: Founder Dependency

nodes.source_location: lines 136500-136780: Introduction / 2 - Why More Effort Stops Working

nodes.label: Founder Operating Patterns
nodes.rationale: Core thesis: founders stall not from lack of strategy or skill but from internal patterns in how they decide, execute under pressure and lead; fixing strategy on top of a broken pattern is fixing the wrong problem.

nodes.label: Four Jobs of the CEO
nodes.rationale: Hire team, train team, equip team (resources plus autonomy and permission to decide and to learn), hold team accountable - then do whatever you want.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Geometric Expansion
nodes.rationale: Jay Abraham's idea: expansion in all areas at the same time; feels like overwhelm; the T1/T2/T3 structure is what made it possible for Taylor.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Hire From 3-5x Larger Businesses
nodes.rationale: Pull experienced hires from businesses 3-5x your size (not Coca-Cola's CMO at $100k/mo); attract them with a big mission and align with profit share plus quarterly/1-year/3-year bonuses for T1/T2. Internal promotion is how businesses most often die.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Key Result Hedge
nodes.rationale: Stack key results so they overshoot the objective (e.g. 270k customers against a 180k target) so hitting them guarantees the objective.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Mario Decision Framework
nodes.rationale: State the exact decision, identify the cost of not deciding, pick the best option with current information, commit and act, inspect and adjust; make repeatable rules for recurring decisions.
nodes.source_location: lines 67290-67340: Introduction: Mario Lanzarotti operating-pattern lessons

nodes.label: Nervous System Regulation
nodes.rationale: The nervous system controls response to pressure, decision speed and handling of stress/conflict; a regulated state gives clear thinking and direct communication, a dysregulated state gives overthinking, delay and avoidance - so 'I know what to do but don't' is a nervous-system problem, not a knowledge problem.

nodes.label: Objectives Key Results Assignments
nodes.rationale: Client Ascension pyramid borrowed from Google OKRs: objectives are large company-wide difficult goals; key results are smaller projects with an outcome and a constraint whose achievement makes hitting the objective impossible to miss; assignments are the individual work items. 2-3 key results per objective, 3-10 assignments per key result; a 'water flow' from T1 to T2 to T3.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Operational Leverage
nodes.rationale: Work happening without the founder - the actual value of a business.
nodes.source_location: lines 137253-137440: Introduction / 5 - Why Your Business Feels Chaotic (And How to Fix It)

nodes.label: Over-Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Founder tries to make everything too right and carries too much, creating dependency.

nodes.label: Permission Seeking

nodes.label: Perpetual Understaffing
nodes.rationale: Engineer an environment where people have almost enough time but not quite; being stretched past normal limits creates flow and forced creativity; surplus makes teams weak (Elon/Twitter example). Higher standards are the greatest gift to A players.
nodes.source_location: lines 138423-141200: Onboarding Operations Systems / Getting Rich Through Other People

nodes.label: Prioritization Over Balance
nodes.rationale: Self first (reading, study, exercise), then family rituals (wake kids daily, weekly dates), then business, then relationships; missed items get backfilled, not sacrificed.

nodes.label: Purchase Time and Labor

nodes.label: Recurring Problem Rule
nodes.rationale: If something happens more than once it should not be solved more than twice: define the standard, the system and the role, then remove yourself.

nodes.label: Systems and People Scaling
nodes.rationale: Replace founder effort with hires, SOPs, standards and delegation; the problem then shifts from capacity to dependency - remove yourself one area at a time by communicating standard, process and consequence.

nodes.label: T1/T2/T3 Team Layers
nodes.rationale: T1 decision makers (outsource the mind; set objectives, manage implementation against key results), T2 managers (set assignments, ensure on time/under budget/in quality; paid to argue with you), T3 laborers (do the work). nodes.label: Three-Question Decision Protocol

nodes.rationale: First step of handling any objection: sniff out smoke screens, then empathize, lower resistance and isolate the single real reason; a direct no beats being left in the dark.

nodes.label: Money Objection
nodes.rationale: 'Money aside, are you confident this gets you to X?' - anything is too expensive if they don't believe; if confident, open an honest finance conversation (smaller package, reallocating other vendor spend).

nodes.label: No Good Reason Tie-Down
nodes.rationale: 'Do you see any reason this wouldn't work for you / get you to X?' - if they can't think of one they default to no, which is a yes; closes without pressure and surfaces the real objection.

nodes.label: Confused Prospects Don't Buy

nodes.source_location: lines 69534-69734: Sales / Million Dollar Pitch Architecture

nodes.label: Current Efforts
nodes.rationale: What they do now, what they tried, what else they are considering - surfaces past agency burns and competitors so the pitch isn't blindsided; tonality on 'nothing' creates urgency.
nodes.source_location: lines 69337-69533: Sales / Bullet Proof Discovery Structure

nodes.label: Discovery Recap
nodes.rationale: Summarize situation, challenges, goals; 'is that fair? anything I haven't covered?' - makes them feel heard and grants permission to pitch.

nodes.label: Expert Perspective
nodes.rationale: Pre-pitch: 'Do you mind if I share some thoughts?' then status-signal credentials and dismantle the #1 limiting belief about the service category, talking about third parties not the prospect so it isn't preachy; no visual needed.
nodes.source_location: lines 69534-69734: Sales / Million Dollar Pitch Architecture

nodes.label: Generate Questions, Not Yes/No
nodes.rationale: Ask 'what are your thoughts/questions on 1-3' instead of 'does that make sense' so you are not pitching to a brick wall and can gauge the prospect.

nodes.label: Goals Clarification
nodes.rationale: Lead vague 'more revenue' answers to a specific measurable point B and get verbal agreement, e.g. $100K/month via 20 calls/month.

nodes.label: Immediate Roadmap and Quick Wins
nodes.rationale: Visual 30/60/90-day (or time-to-value appropriate) roadmap with checkpoints and quick wins; sets realistic expectations so prospects don't invent unrealistic ones, while building excitement.
nodes.source_location: lines 69534-69734: Sales / Million Dollar Pitch Architecture

nodes.label: Investment Presentation
nodes.rationale: Recommend one package, say 'investment' not price, relate it to the end result, say the number and pause briefly, then ask if it aligns with what they can invest to hit the goal; stay cool, calm, confident.
nodes.source_location: lines 69534-69734: Sales / Million Dollar Pitch Architecture

nodes.label: Lean Out
nodes.rationale: When a prospect is indifferent, lean out ('if things are working, what has you looking?') to dig for pain without seeming needy; the person who needs the deal least gets it.
nodes.source_location: lines 70141-70357: Sales / Complete Script Template Breakdown

nodes.label: Limiting Belief Breakdown
nodes.rationale: Identify the one thing the prospect must believe for the pitch to make sense (e.g. cold email needs 5k+/month volume; static ads are a testing mechanism not a video replacement) and solve it at the top instead of over email later.
nodes.source_location: lines 69534-69734: Sales / Million Dollar Pitch Architecture

nodes.label: Making the Prospect Feel Heard
nodes.rationale: People hate unsolicited advice from someone lacking context (doctor/strep analogy); understanding their business makes the pitch welcome rather than disingenuous.
nodes.source_location: lines 69337-69533: Sales / Bullet Proof Discovery Structure

nodes.label: Million Dollar Pitch Architecture
nodes.rationale: Repeatable pitch: discovery recap, permission for perspective, mechanism belief, credibility, 3-4 delivery steps with a visual, 30-90 day roadmap, process questions, ROI tied to goal, confidence check, calm investment statement, next steps, direct ask.

nodes.label: Motivation Question
nodes.rationale: 'What motivated you to book this call today?' asked before business background; often yields half the needed info and prevents talkative prospects burning 10-15 min.
nodes.source_location: lines 69337-69533: Sales / Bullet Proof Discovery Structure

nodes.label: Obnoxiously Persistent Without Seeming Needy
nodes.rationale: Follow up as a professional, not because you need the client; 'just had a minute to follow up' and 'should I close this out?' beat needy or corporate 'circling back' jargon.

nodes.source_location: lines 69337-69533: Sales / Bullet Proof Discovery Structure

nodes.rationale: Whoever asks the questions controls the call (courtroom analogy); many prospect questions are reflexive, so pause and ask why they're asking rather than answering with a diatribe.

nodes.label: Triple A Framework
nodes.rationale: Hormozi's acknowledge / associate / ask: acknowledge to lower sales resistance, associate them with best clients who had the same concern, then ask a question that attacks the frame - people can't disagree with a question and you stay in control.
nodes.source_location: lines 69970-70140: Sales / Perfect Flow Conversation Method

nodes.label: Upbeat Curious Tonality
nodes.rationale: Childlike curiosity keeps reframes from annoying prospects; seek to understand, not to win.
